text:
mira: Heads up — planning to flip cluster-prod-usw2 from nodepools -> Karpenter canary tonight (22:00 UTC). During yesterday's scale test we hit ENI limits in two AZs and saw ~20s pod launch spikes. Need a quick checklist before we start.

devon: +1. Can you paste the error logs/metric you saw?

mira: From cloudwatch: `eni_count` spiked to 78/80 in us-west-2b at 21:12, then we had 12 pending gpu pods for ~35s. Also saw `AttachVolume` errors for some pods.

samir: That matches the repro I got on a kube-conformance run — when karpenter requests lots of heterogeneous instances, ENI allocation can concentrate in one AZ. We should: 1) set `consolidation: disabled` for the canary to avoid aggressive binpacking, 2) pin `requirements` to prefer spread across zones, 3) add `ttlSecondsAfterEmpty` low so we don't accumulate nodes.

mira: Draft of the prov manifest I'm thinking to apply (shortened):
```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: canary-provisioner
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
      operator: In
      values: [us-west-2a,us-west-2b,us-west-2c]
  consolidation: Disabled
  provider:
    subnetSelector: {karpenter: "subnet-usw2"}
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 60
  limits:
    resources: 
      cpu: 2000
```

devon: Two quick asks: annotate the canary nodes with `karpenter.sh/canary=true` so autoscaler policies ignore them, and add a `maxNodeStartup` cap so we don't hammer ENI pools.

lena: For ENI hotspots, we should also pre-warm the ENI quota by creating a small warm pool of gp instances in each AZ. That reduced cold-starts for the previous migration.

arjun: +1 to warm pool. Also suggest running this as a rolling canary: route a single workload (label `karpenter-canary=1`) and run soak for 1h. If ENI>85% in any AZ alert and rollback.

mira: I ran `kubectl get nodes -l karpenter.sh/provisioner=canary-provisioner -o wide` and saw nodes launching across all AZs yesterday but then many were consolidated into 2 AZs after 2m. That consolidation is what likely exhausted ENIs in those AZs.

samir: If consolidation is the culprit, `consolidation: Disabled` + `ttlSecondsAfterEmpty` low should stop aggressive rebalancing. Also set the provider `capacityType` preference (spot vs on-demand) per AZ to avoid mass spot eviction in one AZ.

ops-bot: deploybot: scheduled rollback watcher enabled for canary-provisioner (alerts @mira @devon).

devon: Quick checklist before flip:
- [ ] Apply canary provisioner manifest (with annotations)
- [ ] Create warm pool 3 nodes/AZ (gp3, small)
- [ ] Start canary workload with label `karpenter-canary=1`
- [ ] Run scale test: 50 gpu pods over 10m
- [ ] Watch ENI usage, pod Pending, AttachVolume errors
- [ ] If any AZ ENI >=85% or avg pod launch >30s -> rollback

lena: I'll provision the warm pool and monitor ENI quotas. Sending AWS steps in a sec.

arjun: I'll prepare a temporary quota increase request with infra-aws in case we still hit limits (low-risk path).

mira: Thanks all — planning to start at 22:00 UTC. If anyone sees a better knob we should tweak it now. Otherwise I'll post status updates in this thread during the run. :rocket:
